recipes.name: Kofta Kebabs
ingredients_raw: 28 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes

steps.text: Mash garlic into a paste with salt using a mortar and pestle or the flat side of a chef's knife on your cutting board.
Mix garlic into lamb with onion, parsley, coriander, cumin, cinnamon, allspice, cayenne pepper, ginger, and pepper in a mixing bowl until well blended.

Form mixture into 28 balls. Form each ball around the tip of a skewer, flattening it into a 2-inch oval; repeat with remaining skewers. Place kebabs onto a baking sheet, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 12 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.

Cook skewers on the preheated grill, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 5 to 6 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a kebab should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Kofta Kebabs
raw_recipe.description: Kofta made with ground lamb and aromatic spices, shaped into kebabs and grilled. Serve with pita and yogurt dressing for a delicious Middle Eastern meal.

review.reviewBody: Very good, tastes authentic. I use ground beef instead of lamb and serve with the traditional garlic sauce: 4 gloves of garlic, peeled and crushed, 1/4 c olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, 1/4 teaspoon salt. Process in blender or food processor. If the mixture is too runny, add mayo to thicken it to a creamy-thick consistency. Serve over the koftas.

This was a very good recipe, my family loved it. They even went as far as suggesting that I sell it in a food tent at our local farmers market. Here's the changes I made. I doubled the recipe and used a pound of lamb and a pound of higher quality ground beef. I also added a doubling of the spice mixture to a gallon sized ziplock bag add a ½ cup of water to create a marinade to which I added two pounds of chicken breast. If possible purchase thinly sliced chicken breast or ask the butcher counter to slice it for you. Let the chicken marinade for a minimum of 24 to 48 hours. I also used wood charcoal when I grilled everything it helps add a smokiness to the flavor of the meat.

This recipe was delicious with ground bison. Because the bison is pretty lean, I couldn't get it to stay on skewers, so I remedied that problem by putting a sheet of foil below them and poking the foil with a fork to get the flavor of the grill to come through. I did not have ground coriander, but used a spice mix with coriander as the first ingredient that also contained several other of the listed ingredients. I could not resist adding a little smoked paprika, either. Great with tzatziki; I'm finally getting through my glut of cucumbers.

I tried this recipe and found it addictively delicious. I did find it a little salty and will cut that back a little, as well as the cinnamon, nextime. I skipped the kebab skewers and opted for a stove top skillet. Forming them into sausage sized links that I flattened a bit in the pan. I served them in flour taco shells with tzatsiki and lettuce and tomatoes. I literally ate half of the batch myself. Don't miss this one.

Excellent recipe, great balance on the spices. I did make two small changes.
1. Used 1 lb of veal instead of lamb, because that's what we had in the freezer
2. Divided meat into 12 pieces and doubled them up on the skewers (so, used 6 skewers)
Served with homemade flatbread, and it was an amazing meal.

This recipe was delicious! I did cut back the cinnamon to 1 tsp. Instead of grilling I broiled them just as small 2" patties for 5-6 minutes on top of a broiler pan Excellent with tzaziki and warmed naan bread!

This is a fabulous recipe. I did use beef - can't afford lamb here, it's way too expensive. But the beef was fresh. Also didn't get a chance to grill - went poof on me - so i called a middle eastern friend for baked direction: preheat over to 500, and place koftas (on skewers or not - i left mine on, as they were metal) and bake for about 15-20min. The high heat gives it a fake sear, but they are still really very good. I had mine with some lovely potatoes on garlic naans. Fabulous, and I'm definitely making again now that my grill is back up and running!

I used half and half ground regular and lean beef. I formed the mixture to 24 balls (golf ball size); rolled them to oval shape on a plate with vegetable oil (this way the meat did't get dry); and refrigerated them. I place the balls on flat skewers ( 5 pieces per skewer) right before grilling. This recipe is pretty easy for a beginer like me as most of the ingredients are ground.

I used half beef and half lamb but other wise followed the recipe exactly. Except I made 9 ovals that I cooked on my grill pan for about 7 minutes per side, and also did 7 "tube-shaped" ones on skewers and grilled them on my infrared barbecue for about 9 minutes, turning every 3 or so. I will probably do this again my way because neither cooking method accommodates as many servings as I wanted, but both turned out delicious! I had them in pita bread with tzatziki, onions, tomatoes, and greens and absolutely loved it. The only reason I didn't give the recipe 5 stars is that it took awhile to put together with all that grating and slicing and measuring, but because of the flavor I will definitely make these again!

I love this recipe. The first time I made it I didn't have any lamb so used ground beef as others had done. I followed everything else as per the recipe. For cooking I place 4 of the kebab balls to one large metal skewer. Used ask many skewers as required based on how many servings I required.. This made rotating them during cooking very simple while being able to cook many in one sitting. While the ground beef turned out well the next two times I made them I used lamb and they were awesome. Everyone in the family loves them and will continue to make as per this recipe.

I made a derivative version and there's no turning back. I ground up the spice mix with everything except the lamb, and caked it all over bone-in racks of pork ribs. After marinating overnight, it baked for 45 minutes in the oven at 400F. Absolutely DELICIOUS! I find it takes a double-batch of this mix to properly coat 1 large rack of pork back ribs.
I followed the recipe as written, and served with tzatziki and pita. Lettuce, tomato and onion on the side to build your own. Hit!!!
I’ve been making for years- even better then I had when visiting Turkey

I used 90/10 ground beef and added a handful of currants to the mixture. I shaped the kofta kebabs around cinnamon sticks and broiled for 6-8 minutes, turning halfway. They broiled up perfectly. I served them with rice and potato Tahdig and garlic sauce. For the garlic sauce I followed the recipe of another reviewer for this kebab recipe. It added the perfect finishing touch to my new favorite kebab recipe! I cannot express enough how amazing this recipe is. I have served it at two dinner parties in a row because my guests requested it again!
I really like the consistency of the result regardless of the grind on the lamb and variability of the amounts of ingredients.
Delicious! Used anther reviewers' suggestion for baking in oven: preheat over to 500, and place koftas (on skewers or not - I left mine on, as they were metal) and bake for about 15-20min.

Very good. I had 2 lbs of lamb so I adjusted the ingredients accordingly except kept the amount of cinnamon and coriander the same based on other reviews. Made 12 "logs" and broiled in the oven on metal skewers. Will make again.
Very flavorful and easy to make. I made 8 kebabs from one pound of meat. They must be tiny if you make 28 as the recipe directs.

This is a really good basic recipe for koftas. You can adjust the seasonings to suit your tastes. Instead of making the garlic paste, I grate my fresh garlic on my Microplane grater, which pretty much reduces it to a juicy paste. After my husband complained about maneuvering the skewers on the grill, I began making flat, oval patties, pressing my fingers gently into them to make a sort of 'grilled' look. They cook more easily and quickly, and might even stay a bit juicier. Makes a delicious meal with homemade flatbreads and tzatziki, plus some chopped cucumber and tomato.
I made this with ground beef - excellent! next, I will try half beef/glamb
